hero.title: Know what you're really buying, before you sign.
hero.sub: We pull a flat's official data, cadastre, energy, urban planning, natural risks, neighbourhood, and explain it in plain language. So you decide on facts, not hunches.

trust.title: Official, open sources only
trust.note: No portal scraping. Verifiable, date-stamped data.

catch.title: What a report can surface
catch.note: The kind of thing buyers miss until the notary, or never find at all.

items.title: An affectation on the finca
items.desc: A flat can sit on a building the city has earmarked, one day it could expropriate part of it. We read the Ajuntament's official affectation verdict and explain what it means for you.

items.title: A protected building
items.desc: A heritage listing (BCIN/BCIL) limits what you can change, façade, layout, sometimes the windows. We flag it before it derails your renovation budget.

items.title: Asking far above closing
items.desc: Asking prices run above what flats actually sell for. We show the neighbourhood's recent closing-price range so you can see the gap, and use it to negotiate.

who.title: For people buying a home to live in
who.body: Not investors. Not short-lets. We work only for the buyer, we never sell flats and never take money from sellers. That's why we can tell you what's wrong with a flat, not just what looks nice.

honest.title: We never invent a price
honest.body: No made-up valuation, no black-box estimate. We give you the official €/m² references and the recent closing-price range for the neighbourhood, and let you judge for yourself. Honest beats precise-looking.

partner.title: Work with home buyers?
partner.body: Buyer's agents, mortgage brokers, lawyers and gestories use {brand} to give clients clarity they can trust. Co-branded reports, referrals and API access available.

pricing.title: One price, no surprises
pricing.desc: Free preview. Full report and downloadable PDF for {price}.

items.q: Where does the data come from?
items.a: Official, open sources: Cadastre, ICAEN, Mapa Urbanístic de Catalunya, SNCZI and city-council open data. We don't scrape portals.
We use official, date-stamped sources and say so when something couldn't be verified. It's an orientation tool, not a certificate, we're explicit about the limits in every report.

items.q: Can I use it to negotiate?
items.a: Yes, it's one of the main uses. The price references and any planning or building issues are exactly the facts that move a price.

items.q: Does it replace an architect or lawyer?
items.a: No. It's an orientation tool; it doesn't replace a technical survey, legal review or valuation. Every report says so.
We only need the flat's address to build a report. We don't share it. See the privacy page for the details.
The preview is free. The full report with PDF is {price}, a one-off payment.
For now, yes. We're starting with the city of Barcelona.

footer.disclaimer: Orientation tool. Not a substitute for a technical survey, legal review or valuation.

humility.lead: The range brackets the whole neighbourhood:
humility.body: an unreformed low floor at the bottom, a reformed flat with a balcony at the top. Verify against concrete comparables of similar size, floor and condition before you offer.

unavailable.body: This address falls outside the 73 Barcelona barris we hold registered closing prices for, or too few flats sold here in the last 12 months to publish an average we'd trust. We won't show you a price range we can't stand behind.

howTo.heading: How to read this
howTo.portals: Check current asking prices for similar-size flats nearby on a live portal, and remember asking sits consistently above what flats actually close at.
howTo.askAgent: Ask your agent for recent closed sales on this street or block, the closest thing to a real comparable.
